Certified type:

- Type designations: MUT2300, MUT2200EL, MC406M (electronic converter)
- Description: electromagnetic water meter...

The certified type is "MUT2300 and MUT2200EL with electronic converter MC406M".

Components: electronic converter MC406M could be a component. Role: electronic converter.

Model family:
- Family: two types: MUT2300 (reduced bore) and MUT2200EL (full bore). Additionally meter sizes DN50...DN300.

The models: I'll model per type and meter size? That's a lot: MUT2300 has 9 sizes, MUT2200EL has 9 sizes (DN50 on page 3, and DN65-DN300 on page 4 — table 3 on page 3 has only DN50 row, then page 4 continues the table with DN65...DN300). So MUT2200EL: DN50-DN300 (9 sizes).

Approach: model_family with models like "MUT2300 DN50", "MUT2300 DN65", ..., "MUT2200EL DN50", ..., "MUT2200EL DN300". That's 18 models.

Then model_level characteristics: q1, q2, q3, q4, q3_q1_ratio, diameter_in_outlet (mm), indicating_range_minimum, verification_scale_interval_maximum.

Also matrix_tables: Table 2 (MUT2300 flow rates), Table 3+page4 table (MUT2200EL flow rates), Table 4 (indicating device MUT2300), Table 5 (indicating device MUT2200EL).

Type-level characteristics (Table 1):
- measuring_principle: Electromagnetic
- accuracy_class: 2
- environmental_class: M1 / O (installed outdoors)
- electromagnetic_environment: E1 (remote version), E2 (compact version) — could be config_level with axis "electronic_converter_version". Let me do that: config_level entry: attribute electromagnetic_environment, axis electronic_converter_version, values: [{condition: "remote version", value: "E1"}, {condition: "compact version", value: "E2"}].
- temperature_range_ambient: -25 to +55 °C
- water_temperature_class: T30 (+0.1 °C / +30 °C) — water temperature range 0.1 to 30 °C, class T30. I could record water_temperature_class: "T30" and water_temperature_range min 0.1 max 30 °C.
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa (16 bar) — record value 1.6, unit MPa.
- orientation: All positions
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: U0 and D0 (0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream)
- reverse_flow: designed to measure reverse flow (true/string)
- power_supply: Replaceable battery 2.9–3.7 V → power_supply_voltage: {min 2.9, max 3.7} V; power_supply_type: "Replaceable battery"

Pressure loss class varies by type:
- MUT2200EL: Δp 10 (0.010 MPa or 0.10 bar) for all sizes
- MUT2300: Δp 25 for sizes < DN80, Δp 40 for sizes ≥ DN80 — config_level with axis meter_size.

Let me do config_level for pressure loss:
config_level: [
  {attribute: "pressure_loss_class", axis: "type_and_meter_size", values: [
    {condition: "MUT2200EL, all sizes", value: "Δp 10", ...},
    {condition: "MUT2300, sizes < DN80", value: "Δp 25"},
    {condition: "MUT2300, sizes ≥ DN80", value: "Δp 40"}
  ]},
  {attribute: "pressure_loss", axis: "type_and_meter_size", values: [
    {condition: "MUT2200EL, all sizes", value: 0.01, unit_symbol: "MPa"},
    {condition: "MUT2300, sizes < DN80", value: 0.025, unit_symbol: "MPa"},
    {condition: "MUT2300, sizes ≥ DN80", value: 0.04, unit_symbol: "MPa"}
  ]}
]

Hmm, value with unit symbol — the schema for config_level says values[]: {condition, value}. Rule 5 says "Values follow the same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}". OK.

Software: bootloader versions with CRC checksums, firmware versions. Could record in matrix_tables or as a table. I'll add a matrix_table "Software identification" with columns software, version, crc_checksum.

Test reports:
- NMi-15200444-01, 31 March 2016, 39 pages — role: type_evaluation_report? Actually these are test/examination reports. The cert says "results of tests and examinations provided in the associated report(s)". Roles: the Documentation folder no. T10713-4 is documentation_file. The reports — I'd assign role "test_report" for most. Actually the first one might be the Type Evaluation Report. Not specified. Hmm. The certificate page 1 mentions "OIML Type Evaluation Report". The report NMi-1902198-01 dated 3 December 2018 matches project number 1902198 — that's likely the type evaluation report. But I shouldn't fabricate. I'll assign role "test_report" to all the numbered reports, and documentation_file for T10713-4 folder. Actually the schema says role: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. I could put NMi-1902198-01 as type_evaluation_report since its number matches the project number and date matches issue. That's a reasonable inference but slightly speculative. I'll keep it as test_report to be safe? Hmm. The instructions say don't fabricate. The document doesn't explicitly label any report as the Type Evaluation Report. I'll use "test_report" for all seven, and add documentation folder T10713-4 as documentation_file (explicitly "Documentation folder no. T10713-4").

Recommendation: R49 (canonical "R49"), edition... R49-1 (2013). The recommendation is R49, parts: R49-1, 2013 edition. Schema: id "R49", edition 2013? edition is int. Hmm, edition (int) — for R60 example edition might be like 2000. Here "R49-1 (2013)" — edition 2013. Amendment: null. scheme: "B". accuracy_classes: [2].

Revision history: none present. Omit.

Footnotes: none.

MUT2300: DN50, DN65, DN80, DN100, DN125, DN150, DN200, DN250, DN300
MUT2200EL: DN50, DN65, DN80, DN100, DN125, DN150, DN200, DN250, DN300

model_family: family_name: null (no explicit family name; text says "family of instruments"). Models entries with attributes maybe nominal size and type. I'll include attributes: {"type": "MUT2300", "bore": "reduced", "meter_size": "DN50", "nominal_diameter_mm": 50}. Hmm, keep it modest: attributes with type, bore, meter_size.

Actually schema: models[]: model_id, label, attributes{}. I'll give model_id like "MUT2300-DN50", label "MUT2300 DN50 (reduced bore)", attributes {"type": "MUT2300", "meter_size": "DN50", "bore": "reduced", "diameter_in_outlet": 50 ...}.

Table 4 — indicating device MUT2300:
DN50: indicating range min value 9,999,999 m³? Wait, "Indicating range (minimum value)" — hmm, that's odd: indicating range minimum value 9 999 999? That seems like it should be maximum value of indicating range... Actually for water meters the indicating range is the range of the register. "Indicating range (minimum value)" — perhaps meaning the minimum indicating range (i.e., at least 9999999 m³). And "Verification scale interval (maximum value)".
